messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165573/topic/3766109:

Hi!

Since version 0.5.3, you should find \"Enlarge Font\" and \"Shrink Font\" in the \"View\"-menu, whenever the console is active.

For older versions, permanent settings, or any other specific needs, this setting is pretty well hidden, indeed: The font setting is shared with the script-editor windows. So open a Script File, then select Settings->Configure Editor->Fonts & Colors->Fonts. Note that with some versions of KDE you need to restart RKWard before the setting is applied in the console.

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/3772649:

Ok, I think these are two issues.

First, there are [b]two[/b] input fields. The upper one is for the file-name, the second is used to assign the table a name in R (R supports many tables at once, that\'s why this is needed). The second field should be pre-initialized to \"my.spss.data\". If it\'s red, that is probably because you already have an object by that name. You could check the \"overwrite\"-checkbox, or change the name to \"my.spss.data2\", or something. That \"VAR\"-appearing is an annoying bug, indeed, but it should not prevent you from using the dialog, and it\'s fixed in our development version.

Regarding the upper field, it should be possible to enter the filename, there, manually. To get the button to work, try this: Go to Programs->KDE->System Settings->Advanced->Platform and uncheck \"Use native file dialogs\". Restart RKWard. This is a bug in KDE, which is fixed for KDE 4.5, IIRC.

Does this help?

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Some progress on the Mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

recently several people have tried (and failed) to install RKWard on the Mac. 
Now a friend has given me ssh-access to his mac, and after some trial-and-
error, I have sucessfully compiled rkward on the Mac.

I have not done any decent testing, yet, since working remotely with X11 over 
SSH is painfully slow, but it appears to work, too. Note that rkward hung at 
startup for me twice, which may be due to some Mac or SSH-specific problem. 
Probably there *are* some further problems, and I'll try to investigate those 
as time allows. However, I did not want to wait before letting you know that 
rkward finally *can* be installed on the Mac.

Updated instructions are available at 
https://sourceforge.net/apps/mediawiki/rkward/index.php?title=RKWard_on_Mac .

I believe the key missing step was to run ". /sw/sbin/kde4-buildenv.sh" (note 
the dot and space at the start of the command). You will also need to use an 
up-to-date svn checkout of rkward.

Regards
Thomas

> the rather unstable windows version of rkward (I know I should use Linux,
> but this is my work PC ;-) ), so autosaving would save a lot of hassle. I

the development version of RKWard has support for this (still somewhat buggy 
on windows). Also, sophisticated support for recovering text documents in the 
editor component is under development in the KDE libraries (but probably not 
before KDE 4.6).

Thomas
